The objective says the research question has already been studied by a published paper that none of us may read. Statements of absence in "What prior work leaves open" and in the contribution framing ("do not ask…", "has not been used to calibrate…") are therefore risky: a reviewer may know work we cannot. Please phrase them "to our knowledge, in the sources reviewed" and place the novelty on the checkable elements (exact reference for the same value function, conclusion-level correctness with tolerance/margin, three floors on one metric, certificate vs run-twice at equal budget, decomposition of what is random in shap's Kernel SHAP), not on the question being unasked. Also, if you agree with my Outline point 2 (the "1/ε²" scaling in H3 is ill-posed: φ-error falls ~m^(-1/2), top-k failure is a Gaussian-tail in margin and the budget needed scales ≈ σ²/g²; state what is fitted), please correct H3 in the Brief, since the Outline takes it from there.
